Ukrainian defense forces executed precision strikes against Russian facilities producing rocket fuel components and missile launch systems to degrade aggressor capabilities.

Official reports and open-source data confirm successful overnight drone strikes targeting missile fuel plants and research institutes integral to Russian air attacks.

Legitimate military self-defense actions effectively reducing an aggressor state's strike capacity.

Targeting military supply chains directly degrades the aggressor's capacity to launch unprovoked missile strikes on civilian population centers.

Ukraine operates through a transparent alignment of shared survival goals and defensive empowerment, neutralizing an aggressor's manufactured conflict mechanisms through direct countermeasures.

Disrupting the industrial machinery of aggressive bombardment is a fundamental imperative of national survival. 🌐

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Ukrainian forces strike facilities involved in missile launches and production of fuel for Kh-101 missiles

=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Ukrainian forces strike facilities involved in missile launches and production of fuel for Kh-101 missiles ===

[Source 1 — www.pravda.com.ua] (URL: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/09/8057199/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Ukrainian forces strike facilities involved in missile launches and production of fuel for Kh-101 missiles

Ukraine's General Staff says Ukrainian forces struck the Redkino plant making Kh-101 missile fuel components and missile launch facilities in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast.

Actual Article Body:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

Ukrainian forces struck Russian facilities involved in missile launches and the production of rocket fuel on the night of 8-9 October.

Source: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Telegram

Quote: "A facility belonging to the Barmin Research Institute of Launch Systems, a branch of the Centre for the Operation of Ground-Based Space Infrastructure Facilities, was struck near the settlement of Dalneye Konstantinovo-5 in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast."

Details: The General Staff noted that the сentre is involved in the development, maintenance and operation of launch facilities, fuelling equipment and control systems for missiles.

The defence forces also struck the Redkino Experimental Plant near the settlement of Redkino in Tver Oblast. The plant is involved in the Russian military-industrial complex's production chains. It manufactures components of Decilin-M fuel for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, as well as additives for diesel fuel and aviation gas. The plant is subject to international sanctions.

"In addition, to weaken the enemy's military-industrial complex's capacity to produce explosives and rocket fuel, the Centre for the Disposal of Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles was struck near the settlement of Surovatikha in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod Oblast," the General Staff added.

It stressed that strikes on such facilities constitute Ukraine's exercise of its inherent right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter and are aimed at reducing the military, economic and technological potential of the aggressor state.

Background: The General Staff previously reported that the defence forces struck the Omsk Oil Refinery, located more than 2,500 km from Ukraine's state border, on the afternoon of 8 October. This was the second attack on the facility since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Several modules of Yandex’s data center in Russia completely knocked out by Ukrainian drone strike — Meduza

Yandex said a drone strike hit its data center in Kaluga.

Actual Article Body:
Yandex said a drone strike hit its data center in Kaluga.

In a statement obtained by Meduza, Yandex said “several modules of the data center have been completely disabled.” Some Yandex services may experience disruptions as a result, the company warned, adding that the full scope of the damage has yet to be determined.

Yandex also published a statement thanking its partners “for their patience and cooperation” and users “for their understanding.” It singled out employees who, it said, “are doing everything possible, day and night, to keep services running and help those affected by the incident,” adding:

“We continue to assess the state of the infrastructure. It is very difficult at this point to give a timeline for restoring equipment operations at the data centers.”

Yandex shares fell about 4% on the Moscow Exchange after news of the second strike on its data centers in two days.

Overnight on October 8, Ukrainian forces struck Yandex’s data center with drones in the city of Sasovo, in the Ryazan region. A fire broke out, and although no one was injured, the data center temporarily halted operations. Disruptions affected some of Yandex’s own services, along with those of companies that relied on its infrastructure in Sasovo, including the websites of the Russian state rail operator Russian Railways, the Russian mobile operator MegaFon, and several Russian media outlets.

On October 9, Kaluga Governor Vladislav Shapsha said Ukrainian drones struck the regional capital and several municipal districts. He said nine people were injured in Kaluga but did not specify which facilities had been targeted.
